1174e1d1a4cf117e.title: Environmental health resilience and exposure reduction for healthy aging and longevity
digest: define environmental health resilience factors such as green spaces, age-friendly design and climate-resilient infrastructure as modifiers of exposure–response relationships, which help to explain divergent aging trajectories and offer a framework to advance healthspan equity.

e893aaf338c45d97.title: To understand how social factors shape aging, we need to measure trajectories rather than states
digest: To understand how social disadvantage becomes biologically embedded, aging research must move beyond one-time assessments and instead track continuous, harmonized trajectories of health across the life course.

Measuring both peak attainment and rates of decline — and pairing these with dynamic social exposures — will reveal when and how inequities shape aging, and where intervention can have the greatest effect.

e6f6a222a2cd9b7c.title: Scaling productive aging to mitigate cumulative disadvantage
digest: Productive engagement among older adults — which spans employment, volunteering and family caregiving — functions as a multidimensional driver of healthspan, economic stability and social cohesion across individual and societal levels.
Here we advocate for a paradigmatic shift from observational research towards intersectional, experimental interventions designed to mitigate cumulative, life-course disadvantages.

a18138eaaf865f74.title: Animal models illuminate causal mechanisms of social determinants of aging to advance experimental social geroscience
digest: Social gradients in aging are well known, but their biological basis remains unclear.
Bartolomucci and colleagues discuss data from animal models revealing causal links and molecular pathways of social adversity and introduce the principles of experimental social geroscience.

7d9e9dd83f51cf05.title: Social determinants of health and the exposome shape aging and dementia across global populations
digest: explore how social and environmental conditions across life shape brain aging and dementia through biological pathways, and advance context-sensitive, globally inclusive measures to guide equitable prevention and promote brain health.

b3d209e6d3368191.title: Social isolation, community leisure engagement and the social determinants of healthy aging
digest: Steptoe and Fancourt highlight that community engagement can reduce social isolation, emphasizing the importance of fostering social connections to promote healthy aging and improve health outcomes in older adults.

3633cd280d4bf056.title: Social factors shape health as we age
digest: Our knowledge that social factors can influence health is abundant and has shaped research and policy across medicine, public health and society for decades.

In this special issue, Nature Aging features a collection of reviews and opinion articles that explore how social factors influence healthy aging across the life course and become biologically embedded.
